config.title: mix-blend-mode

intro.title: mix-blend-mode
intro.body: In this lesson, you will create a simple webpage with overlapping text and background elements to explore the visual effects of the CSS `mix-blend-mode` property. You will learn how `mix-blend-mode` controls how an element's content blends with the content or background behind it, similar to layer blending in graphic design software. The core concept involves applying different blend modes—like `multiply`, `screen`, and `overlay`—to see how colors and textures interact. You will use basic HTML for structure and CSS to style and apply the blend modes, focusing on practical visual outcomes. By the end, you'll understand how to use this property to create engaging, blended designs directly in the browser.
intro.usecase: The `mix-blend-mode` property is essential for creating sophisticated visual effects in modern web interfaces. Developers use it to make text or icons legible over dynamic backgrounds, such as hero sections with video or gradient overlays. It's commonly applied in dashboards to blend data visualization layers, in marketing sites for striking image-text compositions, and in UI components like modals or cards to ensure content contrasts elegantly with underlying elements.

objectives: Apply the mix-blend-mode property to HTML elements to control how their colors blend with background content
Configure different blend modes such as multiply, screen, overlay, and difference to achieve specific visual effects
Manipulate text and image elements using blend modes to create layered compositions
Construct interactive examples where blend modes change in response to user actions
Integrate mix-blend-mode with other CSS properties to enhance visual designs
Control blending behavior by adjusting element positioning and stacking context
Implement practical use cases for blend modes including text over images and color correction effects

steps.title: Create the HTML structure for the mix-blend-mode demonstration
steps.instruction: Create a container div with two nested div elements inside it - one for the background layer and one for the foreground text/content layer.
steps.hint: Start with a div element that will serve as the main container. Inside it, add two more div elements - one for the background and one for the foreground content.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a container div with two nested div elements inside it */
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic HTML structure with a container div containing two nested div elements ready for styling with mix-blend-mode.
successCriteria: A container div element exists with two nested div elements inside it - one for background and one for foreground.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly two nested div elements inside the container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what's needed. Create a container div with two nested div elements inside it.

steps.title: Style the container with basic layout properties
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the container div with relative positioning, a width of 400px, height of 300px, and center it horizontally using margin: auto.
steps.hint: Use the .container selector to target the div, then set position: relative, width, height, and margin properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a defined size and be centered on the page, ready for nested elements.
successCriteria: The .container selector has position: relative, width: 400px, height: 300px, and margin: auto.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to include all required properties: relative positioning, width, height, and centering margin.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the CSS rules. The container needs relative positioning, specific dimensions, and horizontal centering.

steps.title: Style the background layer with colors and positioning
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules for the background layer by targeting the .background class. Set its position to absolute, make it fill the entire container with width and height at 100%, and apply a vibrant background color like a linear gradient.
steps.hint: Use absolute positioning to layer the background behind other content. The gradient can be something like: linear-gradient(45deg, #ff6b6b, #4ecdc4).
steps.expectedOutcome: The background layer will be styled with absolute positioning, full dimensions, and a colorful gradient, ready to interact with foreground content.
successCriteria: The .background class has position: absolute, width: 100%, height: 100%, and a background property with a gradient or solid color.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the background layer has all required properties: absolute positioning, full dimensions (100% width/height), and a background color or gradient.
steps.feedbackWrong: The background layer isn't styled correctly. It needs absolute positioning, full container coverage, and a background color or gradient to serve as the base for blend effects.

steps.title: Style the foreground text layer with basic typography
steps.instruction: Add CSS for the foreground text layer by creating a .foreground class selector with absolute positioning, center alignment, large text size, a contrasting color, and appropriate font properties.
steps.hint: Use position: absolute to position the text over the background. Use top: 50% and left: 50% with transform: translate(-50%, -50%) to center it. Set a large font-size and a color that contrasts with the background.
steps.expectedOutcome: The foreground text layer will be styled with absolute positioning, centered, large typography, and a contrasting color ready for blending.
successCriteria: A .foreground selector is created with position: absolute, centering properties (top, left, transform), a large font-size, a contrasting color, and at least one font property like font-weight or font-family.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to include absolute positioning, centering, a large font-size, a contrasting color, and at least one font property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The foreground text layer styling is incomplete or missing. Review the required properties: absolute positioning, centering, large text size, contrasting color, and font properties.

steps.title: Introduce the mix-blend-mode property on the foreground element
steps.instruction: Add the mix-blend-mode property to the existing foreground text layer CSS rule and set its value to 'multiply'.
steps.hint: Look for the CSS rule that styles the foreground text layer and add mix-blend-mode: multiply; to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The foreground text layer will now have the mix-blend-mode property applied with 'multiply' value, creating an initial blending effect with the background.
successCriteria: The .foreground CSS rule contains the property mix-blend-mode: multiply;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added mix-blend-mode: multiply; to the .foreground CSS rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mix-blend-mode property hasn't been added correctly. Look for the .foreground CSS rule and add mix-blend-mode: multiply; to it.

steps.title: Experiment with different blend mode values
steps.instruction: Change the mix-blend-mode value in your .foreground class from its current value to 'screen' to see a different blending effect.
steps.hint: Look for the .foreground selector in your CSS and modify the mix-blend-mode property value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The foreground text will now blend with the background using the 'screen' blend mode, creating a lighter effect compared to 'multiply'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've changed the mix-blend-mode value to exactly 'screen' (without quotes) in the .foreground selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mix-blend-mode value in the .foreground selector should be 'screen'. Please check your CSS syntax and try again.

steps.title: Try overlay blend mode for more complex interactions
steps.instruction: Change the mix-blend-mode value in the .foreground selector from 'screen' to 'overlay'.
steps.hint: Look for the .foreground class in your CSS and update the value inside the mix-blend-mode property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The foreground text will now use the 'overlay' blend mode, which combines both darkening and lightening effects based on the background colors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're updating the mix-blend-mode property in the .foreground selector specifically, and that the value is exactly 'overlay'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. You need to modify the existing .foreground selector to use 'overlay' as the mix-blend-mode value.

steps.title: Test difference blend mode for high-contrast effects
steps.instruction: Change the mix-blend-mode value from 'screen' to 'difference' on the .foreground element to see how it creates inversion effects by subtracting colors.
steps.hint: Look for the .foreground selector in your CSS and update the mix-blend-mode property value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The foreground text will now use the 'difference' blend mode, creating high-contrast inversion effects where overlapping colors are subtracted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're updating the mix-blend-mode property on the .foreground selector to 'difference'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. You need to change the mix-blend-mode value to 'difference' on the .foreground element.

steps.title: Add a second background element to demonstrate layering
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a middle layer element with a different background color and absolute positioning.
steps.hint: Create a new class selector for the middle layer, give it a distinct background color (like a gradient or pattern), and position it absolutely within the container.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for a middle layer element is added with a distinct background and positioning.
successCriteria: A new CSS class selector is created with a background property different from the existing layers and absolute positioning.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a middle layer, but make sure it has both a distinct background property and absolute positioning to properly demonstrate layering.
steps.feedbackWrong: The middle layer CSS rule is missing or incomplete. Create a new class selector with a background property and absolute positioning.

steps.title: Create interactive controls to switch between blend modes
steps.instruction: Add a set of HTML radio buttons inside the container to allow selecting different blend modes (multiply, screen, overlay, difference). Use the :checked pseudo-class to apply the corresponding mix-blend-mode value to the foreground element.
steps.hint: Create radio buttons with unique IDs and matching labels. Use the :checked pseudo-class with adjacent sibling selectors to target the .foreground element and change its mix-blend-mode property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The learner will add HTML radio buttons and corresponding CSS rules that use the :checked pseudo-class to dynamically change the mix-blend-mode value of the foreground element when different buttons are selected.
successCriteria: Radio buttons for multiply, screen, overlay, and difference blend modes are present. CSS rules use the :checked pseudo-class with appropriate selectors to apply the corresponding mix-blend-mode values to the .foreground element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the required elements. Make sure you have radio buttons for all four blend modes and CSS rules that use the :checked pseudo-class to change the mix-blend-mode property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interactive controls are not properly implemented. You need to add radio buttons for the blend modes and CSS rules that use the :checked pseudo-class to dynamically apply different mix-blend-mode values.
